clue.text: Women in bed with cad involved our erstwhile agony aunt

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scandalous tale of a bounder in bed with women, told by a former advice columnist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles all of WOMEN IN BED and CAD; 'with' only joins. The former Conservative minister wrote an agony-aunt column for the Guardian, hence 'our'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ex-MP once answered readers' personal problems in this newspaper, the role of an agony aunt.

indicators.note: driven mad suggests the letters are sent haywire and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some men have been pushed to insanity, and the speaker shrugs it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive idioms saying something does not matter.

parts.note: drinkers who have given up spirits might stick to the grape instead, and street drunks favour cheap fortified plonk

explanation.definitionFit: Habitual drinkers of cheap wine are alcoholics whose tipple is not spirits.

clue.text: Hold your water! What's up, cat died?

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting the pieces up reads them from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a puma is a big wild cat

explanation.surface: Someone panics on learning a pet cat has died and is told to stop crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's up' turns the whole of PUMA plus D to read from the bottom. 'Hold your water' sounds like a plea not to cry; it is an instruction to hold back water as a barrier would.
explanation.definitionFit: To block a river with a barrier is to hold back its water.

indicators.note: but not firm tells us the firm's letters are removed from the constant

parts.note: in maths a coefficient is a constant multiplier
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Someone is described as diligent and steady though not strict.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorough and efficient both describe work done competently with nothing missed.

clue.text: Prayer given a lift from Rome

definitions.meaning: the Lord's Prayer, opening words of which are used as its name
in Latin the prayer is the Paternoster, and a paternoster is also a lift of continuously moving open cars

explanation.surface: A traveller is driven home from the Italian capital, praying.
explanation.walkthrough: A paternoster is a lift with a chain of open compartments that never stops; the name comes from the Latin opening of this prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord's Prayer is known by its opening words in English.

clue.text: Cup bearer that is held up in Mozambique

indicators.note: held means kept within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bra is a garment that holds cups

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A servant who carries goblets is detained somewhere in southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup bearer' looks like a wine-pourer but is a garment that bears cups; 'up' turns the abbreviation for 'that is' round in this down clue, and 'held' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Beira is a port city on the coast of Mozambique, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: One could be adept: him or her?

definitions.text: One could be adept: him or her?

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might become something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A skilled person is asked whether they are male or female.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ADEPT HIM OR HER, and the whole clue also describes the answer: a being with both male and female parts could be called him or her.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism with both male and female sex organs could be referred to by either pronoun.

parts.note: Aurora is Sleeping Beauty, woken by a prince's kiss, and 26 is reviving someone, as first aiders do with mouth-to-mouth

explanation.walkthrough: Aurora is the princess in Tchaikovsky's Sleeping Beauty; the fairy-tale kiss and first aid's mouth-to-mouth both bring someone round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouth-to-mouth rescue breathing is popularly called this, and a kiss revives the sleeping princess.

clue.text: Poison letter carrier to run from French address

indicators.note: run from means the running word is taken away from the letter carrier

parts.note: an envelope carries a letter
to lope is to run with long strides
nom is French for name, the word one addresses someone by

explanation.surface: A postman flees after poison is found in a letter from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter carrier' looks like a postman but is ENVELOPE; removing LOPE leaves ENVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to put venom into something, to make it toxic.

clue.text: Stock the catch in vessel? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
on the contrary reverses the stated roles, so the vessel goes in the catch rather than the catch in the vessel

parts.note: fish are the catch of an angler
an urn is a vessel, a large vase

explanation.surface: A fisherman wonders whether to keep the day's catch in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the vessel would hold the catch; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles so the catch holds the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To stock a room is to supply it, as one does when furnishing it.

definitions.meaning: Thomas More wrote Utopia, so the Utopian's possessions are ...
customs or conventions of a society

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas More wrote Utopia; the Latin word for customs happens to match his name with a possessive S.
explanation.definitionFit: Mores are the customary conventions of a community, its habits.

clue.text: How RU selectors shoulder defensive advice?

definitions.text: How RU selectors shoulder defensive advice?

parts.words: How RU selectors shoulder defensive advice?
parts.note: rugby union selectors must choose a back, and carrying someone on one's shoulders is done in a way with a similar name

explanation.walkthrough: RU is Rugby Union, where backs are the players behind the scrum; a child carried on the shoulders rides in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying someone on one's back or shoulders is a piggyback ride, also called by this name.

indicators.note: sustaining means holding up, so the pianos piece holds the band inside it

parts.note: p is the musical notation for piano, quiet, so two pianos give PP
a rim is a band round the edge of a wheel

explanation.surface: A tuner adjusts pianos while a group keeps playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sustaining' sounds like a piano's pedal but means holding RIM within the two Ps.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to make small adjustments to one's appearance, to tweak it.

clue.text: Wasting time upstairs, Pa! Messing about together

indicators.note: messing about suggests the remaining letters are jumbled
wasting time means losing the time letter from the words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child scolds their father for idling about upstairs when they should be doing things as one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasting' removes T from UPSTAIRS, giving UPSAIRS; 'Messing about' rearranges that with PA.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means side by side, at an equal rate, so together.

parts.note: running costs of a business, and a hat-maker's work goes over customers' heads

explanation.definitionFit: Fixed business running costs are known as these, and a hatter's products sit on top of heads.

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A text may contain a character resembling Roth's famous protagonist.
explanation.walkthrough: Portnoy, of Philip Roth's novel Portnoy's Complaint, is notorious for masturbation.
explanation.definitionFit: Roth's Portnoy is famously given to self-abuse, which this adjective describes.

clue.text: Plateau elevated on mountain with tail pieces

indicators.note: tail pieces means the word tail broken up and reassembled
in a down clue elevated means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: Something is raised on a peak with bits of tail attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' scrambles TAIL to ALTI; 'elevated' turns ON plus ALP into PLANO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Altiplano is the high Andean plateau of Bolivia and Peru, and the word means high plain.

parts.note: a bird whose chest is clearly not blue but another colour

explanation.definitionFit: This is a name for the robin, a bird with a red chest rather than a blue one.

indicators.note: house left means the house letters depart from the name

parts.note: Admiral Nelson's first name was Horatio

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson's home was bequeathed to a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nelson's' means his first name, not his home; 'house left' removes HO from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is a relation between two quantities.

parts.note: the saying that appearances can mislead, applied to the American illusionist's stunts

explanation.walkthrough: David Blaine is an American magician and endurance performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says appearances are misleading, which fits an illusionist's shows.

indicators.note: left in charge places the letter for left within the charge word

parts.note: a person in your care is your charge

explanation.surface: A nun has been put in charge of things.
explanation.walkthrough: St Clare founded the Poor Clares, an order of nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: A Poor Clare is a nun of the Franciscan order founded by St Clare.

indicators.note: of here says the name is taken out of the quoted title, sitting inside its words

explanation.surface: Asks who painted a picture of the legendary British king's trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Max Ernst was a German Surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a Dada and Surrealist painter.

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
pal means friend

explanation.definitionFit: Copal is a resin exuded by tropical trees, so an exudation.

definitions.meaning: to be good enough, make the grade
a film editor trims footage, so would chop the reel

explanation.definitionFit: To be up to the job is to be good enough, to succeed.

clue.text: In which train times are disrupted!

definitions.text: In which train times are disrupted!

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time, so times are TS

explanation.surface: A grumble about a journey where the timetable falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' jumbles TRAIN with TS; the whole clue describes travel while the trains run late.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of travelling from place to place, when timetables may be upset.

parts.note: a British emphatic yes meaning very much so, and literally the opposite of only partly

explanation.walkthrough: In British speech this phrase is an emphatic yes: 'Did you enjoy it?' 'Rather!'
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British reply meaning very much indeed, so fully keen.

clue.text: Thus one brings around a summons from the Nazarene: "Justice for the king!"

indicators.note: the king for Justice means one letter replaces the other

parts.note: Jesus of Nazareth
J is the abbreviation for justice, a judge's title
R is for Rex, king
a citation is a summons to appear in court

explanation.surface: Christ's call to Lazarus to rise is likened to a royal legal ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the J of JESUS for R to get RESUS, then add CITATION. Jesus's summons famously revived Lazarus.
explanation.definitionFit: Resuscitation is reviving someone, the means by which one brings them round.
